title: 3 County News Review football teams win Wednesday - NewsBreak
text:
20 minutes ago
The three teams in the County News Review’s readership area that played on Wednesday, Oct. 21 all were winners.
Cambridge-Isanti posted a home win over Irondale, while North Branch doubled up on a Hermantown and Braham claimed a wild victory over Ely.
Here is a look at all three games.
Bluejackets blast Irondale in home finale
Cambridge-Isanti senior Peyton Coplan ran for 253 yards and four touchdowns to lead the Bluejackets to a 46-22 home victory over Irondale.
Coplan scored on runs of 2 and 16 yards in the first period as the Bluejackets led 16-0 after one quarter, then added a 53-yard run early in the second before junior Knox Andrus caught a 54-yard touchdown pass from senior Tayton Westphal that made the score 29-8 at halftime.
Coplan then took a lateral from Westphal and scored from 41 yards out on C-I’s first drive of the second half to make the score 36-16.
Senior Mason McKinnon kicked a 15-yard field goal before senior Grant Oliver scored on a 7-yard run midway through the fourth quarter to close the scoring.
With the win, Cambridge-Isanti entered the playoffs with a 4-4 record.
Braham, Londgren outscore Ely
Senior David Londgren ran for 258 yards and four touchdowns on 32 carries to lead the Bombers to a wild 40-38 home win over Ely.
Londgren scored on a 6-yard run for the only points of the first quarter, then added TD runs of 9 and 8 yards as Braham led 24-14 at halftime.
He then added a 2-yard scoring burst in the third quarter before sophomore Eli Benzen added a 28-yard TD run early in the final period to cap the scoring for the Bombers.
Braham improves to 5-3 on the season with the victory.
North Branch doubles up Hermantown
The Vikings got three touchdowns from Cohen Baker as they rambled to a 32-16 home victory over Hermantown.
Nolan Bahr got North Branch on the board when he scored on a 20-yard run on the game’s first drive, and Baker scored from 20 yards out late in the second quarter to give the Vikings a 16-8 advantage at halftime.
Baker then added a 14-yard scoring burst at the 5:28 mark of the third quarter before finding the end zone from two yards out late in the game.
North Branch will enter playoff action with a 4-4 overall record.
